source: MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture, banana cultivation techniques manual, 2019, section IV.2 (weeding)
text: Starting about one month after planting, keep the area immediately around each clump (roughly one to two hoe-widths out) clear of weeds. This is typically needed 2-3 times over the course of a year, most importantly during the second and third months while the young plant is still establishing and cannot yet out-compete weeds for light and nutrients on its own; once the canopy closes over, weed pressure naturally decreases. Weeding should be done carefully by hand or hoe rather than deep cultivation, since banana's feeder roots are shallow and easily damaged by aggressive digging near the base. Some farmers use herbicide for weed control between rows, but the source cautions that this should be matched to the farmer's experience and used carefully to avoid harming the crop.
